newsitem.title: USA: Hepatitis A usually clears up in 2-8 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Hepatitis A usually clears up in 2-8 weeks.

text.p: Hepatitis A, linked on Wednesday to a batch of tainted frozen strawberries supplied for school lunches in six U.S. states, typically makes people feel sick for two to eight weeks but is very rarely fatal.
The virus usually clears within about two months, although there are a few rare cases when people develop liver failure that can be fatal.
But the patient often has muscle and joint pain, fever, headache, weakness, nausea and loss of appetite. People often feel tired and lack energy for weeks or months. Some develop jaundice.

Hepatitis A is fairly common in developing countries, where public health and sanitation facilities are poorer. The virus is spread by poor personal hygiene or when food or water is contaminated by sewage.

Other forms of hepatitis, hepatitis B and C, are spread through infected blood and sexual activity. Those viruses have a higher risk of causing chronic liver disease and lethal liver failure, but tests have been developed to detect it in the blood supply, so the risk of contracting them through transfusion has been minimized.
A Centers for Disease Control spokeswoman said there are an estimated 140,000 cases of hepatitis A in the United States each year,and the last major outbreak was in 1989.
